subject: Novapulse: private/on-prem deployment assurance and operator segregation Q&A
body:
From: Alicia Howard <alicia.howard@novapulse.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: Novapulse Compliance <compliance@novapulse.com>, Novapulse Procurement <procurement@novapulse.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: operator boundaries, media handling, and emergency patching for on-prem/private deploy

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for walking us through Redwood's private deployment options yesterday. Our security and procurement teams have a short RFI focused on operator separation, removable media handling, and emergency patch procedures for air-gapped/on-prem installs.

Can you provide:
- a short description of operator roles and which tasks require vendor access vs. customer-only access;
- how removable media (USBs, external drives) are handled for patching and software updates in an air-gapped site;
- your emergency patch process (timeline, verification, chain-of-custody) and whether we can witness or audit that process; and
- any artifacts you can share (diagrams, runbooks, checklists).

We are on a compressed timeline for procurement; a consolidated response by EOD Friday (4/24) would be ideal.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Howard
Head of Vendor Security, Novapulse Health
---

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Alicia Howard <alicia.howard@novapulse.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 11:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: operator boundaries, media handling, and emergency patching for on-prem/private deploy

Hi Alicia —

Thanks for the clear list — we're happy to consolidate. Attached are three artifacts that address the items you listed: an operator separation diagram, a media-handling playbook for air-gapped sites, and a short RFI summary spreadsheet. High-level answers below; we'll follow up with more detail and proposed SOW language if helpful.

1) Operator roles and scope
- Customer Operators: Responsible for day-to-day system administration, network configuration, and physical access. They hold the primary keystores and local KMS integration.
- Vendor (Redwood) Site Ops: Scoped to build-time installation, emergency remediation, and optionally periodic upgrades. Access is gated by customer-controlled bastion and jumpbox, just-in-time (JIT) sessions, and multi-party approval where required.
- Remote support is never provided with persistent credentials — access is session-limited and logged. We recommend a separation where all production data-plane operations remain under customer operators; Redwood’s actions are limited to runtime binary installs, emergency patches, and kernel/runtime troubleshooting.

2) Removable media and updates
- For fully air-gapped sites, we use signed, checksum-verified update artifacts delivered on encrypted media. The media-handling playbook (attached) defines: pre-shipping integrity checks, sealed packaging, acceptance checks at arrival, chain-of-custody forms, and local verification steps (hash checks, signature verification) before any installation.
- All installable artifacts are signed with Redwood's release key; customers can opt to run an independent signature check with their own root-of-trust.

3) Emergency patch process
- Triage window: initial response within 2 business hours of a critical report; patch build and verification targeted within 48 hours for critical fixes (subject to reproducer availability and testing).
- Verification: patches are tested against a minimal reproducible env internally; test results, CVE references, and a checklist are provided to the customer prior to delivery.
- Delivery: patches are staged as signed artifacts on encrypted media for air-gapped installs. Chain-of-custody forms and a tamper-evidence checklist accompany the media.
- Auditability: customers can request a witnessed transfer (on-site) or encrypted artifact transfer with third-party attestation. We maintain detailed logs of all JIT sessions, transfer handoffs, and artifact signatures for 24 months by default (retention adjustable).

Attachments: operator-separation-diagram.pdf, media-handling-playbook.md, rfi-response-summary.xlsx

I'll loop Ben and Grace for anything operational we should add to the SOW. If you want, we can share a redlineable SOW snippet for media-handling and operator scoping by Thursday.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: RFI: operator boundaries, media handling, and emergency patching for on-prem/private deploy

Soojin —

Quick notes on the artifacts:
- Diagram: add explicit flow for who performs HSM seal/unseal during install (customer only by default; vendor allowed if escrow agreed).
- Playbook: include a 3-person signoff for media acceptance at site (carrier + customer ops + vendor rep) for higher-assurance installs.
- Patch SLAs: we should avoid hard 48-hour commitments for zero-day kernel work — propose language that distinguishes application-level vs. kernel/firmware updates.

I can draft SOW language for the above and drop into the shared Drive link.

-ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

> Thanks Ben — good call. Grace, do you have any concerns on operator handoff or auditability we should call out?

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI: operator boundaries, media handling, and emergency patching for on-prem/private deploy

Agree with Ben's caveats. A couple of additions:
- Include a clause that customer may require a cold-boot integrity check (hash of boot image) before any patch is applied. We have that workflow documented in the playbook but should call it out in the SOW.
- For long-term retention of transfer logs, propose an SLA-backed archival window option (default 24 months, premium 60 months).

I'll prepare a redline for the SOW and proposed language for the procurement team.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFI: operator boundaries, media handling, and emergency patching for on-prem/private deploy

Alicia —

Attached is a consolidated response addressing your four bullets, plus a short SOW excerpt covering: operator roles, HSM handling guidance, media acceptance signoff, emergency patch tiers, and audit/retention options. Highlights:
- Vendor access: JIT, logged, session-limited, and removable after tasks complete.
- Media handling: sealed, signed artifacts delivered on encrypted carriers; three-party acceptance recommended for higher assurance.
- Emergency patching: triage in 2 hours, app-level patch delivery targeted within 48 hours; kernel/firmware cadence subject to reproducibility and test window (we will define higher-assurance windows in SOW).
- Auditability: on-site witnessing available; transfer logs and session records retained by default for 24 months. Premium archival available.

Next steps: if the above aligns, we can send a redlined SOW and a procurement-ready quote. Ben will attach the SOW snippet and proposed procurement language in the Drive link.

Thanks for the timeline — happy to set a call next week to walk the compliance team through the artifacts.

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
